core.verdict: The core is genuinely solid: fault isolation works exactly as advertised (verified with throwing upgrade + throwing building unlock, 500 bot ticks, errors logged, both disabled after 3 failures, game unaffected), the cost/maxAffordable/sell math is exact, the accumulator loop hands excess catch-up to the offline path correctly, and performance is far beyond what the game needs. Zero errors attributable to the module. It misses the 8.5 bar on polish, not correctness: fmt() prints \"$1000K\"/\"1000M\" at every magnitude boundary (a visible flicker in the money/income/cost readouts that a premium release would not ship), and core loadState/mergeInto is prototype-pollution-unsafe on its own, currently protected only by the save module's scrub. Both are small, precisely located fixes; with them applied this module would pass at ~8.8.
issues: [medium] src/core/format.js fmt(): at every suffix boundary the rounding step overflows the mantissa. fmt(999950)..fmt(999999) => "1000K" (should be "1.00M"); same for 999.95M => "1000M", 99.95K => "100.0K"-style overshoots at the toFixed(1) tier, and 9.995 => "9.99" (toFixed binary artifact). Verified in scratchpad/edge.mjs. Because fmt drives money, income/s and every building cost in the header/build list, players see "$1000K" flicker each time a number crosses a magnitude boundary. → In fmt after computing v = n / 1000**e, round first then re-normalize: `let s = v >= 100 ? v.toFixed(0) : v >= 10 ? v.toFixed(1) : v.toFixed(digits); if (Number(s) >= 1000) { e++; v = n / Math.pow(1000, e); s = v.toFixed(digits); }` (and handle e reaching SUFFIX.length by falling through to the exponential branch). Add a unit assertion fmt(999999)==='1.00M'.

[medium] src/core/state.js mergeInto()/loadState() is prototype-pollution-unsafe on its own: loadState(JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"pwned":1}}')) set Object.prototype.pwned = 1 (verified in scratchpad/edge.mjs; also via buildings.__proto__). Today the only caller (src/save/index.js applyState) scrubs BAD_KEYS first, so the shipped path is safe, but the core function is exported as a general 'replace state with obj' API and any future caller (import dialog, dev console, tools) that skips scrub() pollutes the global prototype. loadState also accepts wrong-typed sections (log:'notarray', stats.totalEarned:'x', prestige:null) that would make addLog() throw; again only save's coerceShape prevents it. → In mergeInto skip keys `__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype` (3-line guard: `if (k === '__proto__' || k === 'constructor' || k === 'prototype') continue;`) and only recurse when `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(dst, k)`. Extend sanitize() to enforce the createInitialState() shape for log (Array), stats/prestige/settings (objects with finite numbers) so core is safe without relying on save/index.js.

[low] src/core/api.js maxAffordable() log-formula can overshoot by 1 due to float error when money sits within ~1e-13 relative of an exact n-purchase cost: in 60,000 boundary-sampled trials, 359 (0.6%) returned n whose buildingCost(count,n) > money, and buy(id,'max') then returned false doing nothing (the UI 'Max' button in src/ui/build.js:172 would appear dead). Incidence with realistic money values is effectively zero (0/400,000 uniform trials), so this is a robustness nit, not a live bug. → After computing n in maxAffordable add `while (n > 0 && buildingCost(def, count, n) > money) n--;` (or in buy(): `if (n==='max') { n = maxAffordable(def); while (n > 0 && buildingCost(def,count,n) > state.res.money) n--; }`).

[low] src/core/format.js fmtInt() only routes n < 1e6 through toLocaleString, so negatives of any magnitude fall into the locale branch: fmtInt(-1e40) prints a 41-digit comma string and fmtInt(-0.5) prints "-1" (Math.floor). Not currently reachable from UI (peakPop/built/clicks are non-negative) but the helper is public. → Use `Math.abs(n) < 1e6 ? Math.trunc(n).toLocaleString('en-US') : fmt(n)`.

[low] src/core/registry.js validate() checks presence but not numeric sanity of baseCost/costGrowth/cost: costGrowth <= 0 or baseCost <= 0 would make buildingCost/maxAffordable produce NaN/Infinity (log of negative, division by g-1 = -1). derived.costMult is protected by `|| 1` in api.js but a per-building cost mod of 0 (`?? 1` allows 0) yields free buildings and maxAffordable = NaN/10000 depending on money. → In validate(): require Number.isFinite(baseCost) && baseCost > 0, Number.isFinite(costGrowth) && costGrowth >= 1, Number.isFinite(cost) && cost >= 0. In mods.js sanitizeMods treat cost <= 0 (not just < 0) as 1 for the top-level and byBuilding cost fields.
issuesLeftAfterFix: `node tools/economy-sim.mjs --ticks 216000 --out logs/sim-fix-core.json` reports FAIL (errors=0, but [stall]/[flat] issues: money ~1e119, income ~2e72/s, legacy ~9e123 after 38 prestiges). This is NOT caused by core: I copied the project to the scratchpad, reverted my core changes there, and the sim produced byte-identical numbers (money=5.384e107, legacy=7.717e112, issues=24). Root cause is an in-flight cross-module seam being edited concurrently by other builders: src/simulation/tuning.js (18:54) introduced DEFAULTS.prestige.legacyPower=3 / firstBonus=0.5 (income multiplier now (1+0.04*legacy)^3, documented in prestige.js assuming exponent 0.35), while src/balance/config.js (18:52) still ships prestige.exponent=0.5 and no legacyPower/firstBonus keys, so legacy gain and the cubic multiplier compound into a runaway. Fix belongs to simulation/balance (either set config.prestige.exponent to 0.35 and add legacyPower/firstBonus to config, or drop legacyPower back to 1); I did not edit those folders because they were being modified while I worked. sim-fix-upgrades.json from the same minute shows the same runaway.
Critic's UI issues (toasts, aria-live on #app, contrast, clipping, tab wrap, power-bar color, city-hint, Google Fonts) are outside src/core and untouched.

balance.verdict: The first prestige cycle and the next eleven are premium-quality pacing — a purchase every ~5 s, no gap over 42 s, all content reached inside 50 min, cadence shrinking 50 → 5.8 min — but the config breaks past 3.6 h: linear uncapped pollution pins happiness at the 0.25 floor, the 0.35 prestige exponent with a linear legacy bonus makes cycles balloon 5.8 → 117 min, and the upgrade ladder is exhausted, leaving 39 flat-income stretches. Zero errors, but two real late-game gameplay flaws keep it below 8.5; both have config-only fixes verified here (pollutionCap/pollutionCurve 1.0, exponent 0.5) that would lift it to pass territory.
issues: [high] Happiness collapses to the 0.25 floor in the late game and the civic lever stops working. config.happiness.pollutionScale 0.2 applies a LINEAR, uncapped pollution penalty while civicBonus saturates at civicCap 1.25: at the 12 h city (123 factories, 129 coal, 112 refineries) pollution = 2.39 > 1 + 1.25 + 0.1, so happiness sits at the floor from cycle 21 (~6 h) onward and drifts down from cycle 13; income declines inside late cycles (e.g. cycle 12 peak 1.19e8 → 1.10e8) and all 39 sim 'flat' warnings occur after 3 h. The config comment only scopes the scale to '90 minutes of greedy play'. → In src/balance/config.js happiness block add `pollutionCap: 1.0, pollutionCurve: 1.0` (src/resources/math.js pollutionPenalty already supports both; resources reads them each tick). Verified by mutating config in memory: min happiness after 10 min goes 0.25 → 0.52, never floors in 12 h, final income 4.0e9 → 1.27e10. Update the pollutionScale comment to describe the saturating curve.

[high] Prestige cadence reverses instead of accelerating: after cycle 12 (3.6 h) durations grow 5.8 → 6 → 7.2 → 8.4 → 9.2 → 8.7 → 11.7 → 16.5 → 24.2 → 36 → 54.2 → 80 → 117.4 min, then a 139-min cycle never completes. With config.prestige.exponent 0.35 the earnings needed for a meaningful (+25%) legacy haul grow as (0.25·L)^2.86 while income only grows ×(1 + 0.04·L); a fixed-gain player gets shrinking cycles only because each reset becomes worthless (+5 legacy at L=2779 is +0.18% income). → Set config.prestige.exponent 0.35 → 0.5 (the DESIGN.md default). Verified in memory: cycles keep shrinking to 2.0 min at ~2.5 h, 46 prestiges in 12 h (vs 24), final legacy 265k, final income 7.5e11/s; combined with the pollution cap: 49 prestiges, 3.0e12/s. Cycles still lengthen after ~3 h under any config value because incomePerLegacy is additive-linear — to keep cadence accelerating, applyPrestigeMods (src/simulation/prestige.js) needs a compounding bonus (e.g. ×1.02^legacy with a soft cap) or legacy needs a spend sink; flag as a design follow-up outside config.

[medium] Content horizon ends at ~3 h of a 12 h run. 40/41 upgrades are owned by cycle 9; the legacy ladder (legacy-archive $5k, founders-blueprints $30k, veteran-planners $80k, dynasty-ledger $150k) is fully bought by cycle 3; AI Governance ($5e7) and Planetary Charter ($5e8), described in config.js as 'the horizon', are bought around cycle 9. From then on every cycle is buy-the-same-20-buildings with income flat to declining (39 'flat' flags). → Add late legacy rungs to config.upgrades (and matching entries in src/upgrades/data.js gated on legacy ≥ 50 / 250 / 1000 at $1e7 / $1e9 / $1e11), and re-price ai-governance to ~$5e8 and planetary-charter to ~$2e10 so they land in cycles 15–20 rather than 9.

[low] Opening 80 s is the only slow stretch: startMoney $210 is spent in 4 s on 5 buildings, then income is $0.8–1.1/s against $50–58 items, giving waits of 38 s (4 s → 42 s) and 42 s (42 s → 84 s) before the first shop; first upgrade lands at 116 s, not the '~66 s' the config.js header claims. Cookie Clicker gets the first purchase moving within ~15 s. → Raise config.economy.startMoney 210 → 260 (or drop shop baseCost 50 → 35) so the $50 shop is affordable in the opening spree and the first paycheck starts at ~5 s; correct the header comment to the measured 116 s.

[low] The brownout mechanic is nearly invisible to a careful player: powerRatio never drops below 0.957 in 12 h (1.3% of steps < 1, 2.8% in cycle 0), the DESIGN.md 'first brownout ~3 min' beat never happens in the sim, and Smart Grid — the only never-purchased item — cannot unlock without one (its unlock is milestone 'brownout' or powerRatio < 1). The browser bot does trip it (8% share), so this is partly a bot artifact. → Give smart-grid a second unlock path in src/upgrades/data.js (`derived.powerDemand >= 20`, i.e. when coal unlocks) so a competent player still sees it; optionally raise config.buildings.windmill.costGrowth 1.5 → 1.6 so the windmill→coal gap creates a brief, visible brownout around minute 3.

[low] Documentation drift: config.js header says first upgrade ~66 s (measured 116 s) and cycles '48 → 25 → 21 → 17 → 16 → 14' (measured 49.9 → 26.4 → 21.6 → 19.7 → 17.3 → 15.1); DESIGN.md pacing paragraph still says $1M at 35–50 min and 1k pop ~8 min (measured 20.5 min and 12.8 min). → Update the config.js header to the measured values (first upgrade 116 s, 1k pop 12.8 min, $1M 20.5 min, first prestige 49.9 min, cycle list above) and replace the DESIGN.md pacing paragraph with a pointer to those numbers.

resources.verdict: The math is correct, pure, fast and defensively coded; every DESIGN.md formula verified exactly and every edge case degrades gracefully with zero errors. It fails the 8.5 bar on one real gameplay flaw the sim exposes: capped civic bonus versus uncapped linear pollution pins happiness at the 0.25 floor for the back half of every prestige cycle, flattening income (the 39 sim 'flat' issues). The saturation hook already exists in math.js; turning it on by default plus syncing the stale DEFAULTS mirror would move this to 8.5+.
issues: [high] Late-game happiness degenerates to the 0.25 floor. The civic bonus saturates at config.happiness.civicCap (1.25) while the pollution penalty is linear and uncapped (pollutionPenalty returns x when no cap). In logs/sim-gauntlet.json happiness sits at exactly 0.25 for the last ~10 game-hours (e.g. final 129 coal + 123 factory + 112 refinery = Sum 11.93 x pollutionScale 0.2 = 2.39 penalty vs max +1.25 civic). That pins the income multiplier at 0.625x and pop growth at 0.25x, which is what the sim's 39 'flat income' issues late in every prestige cycle are. The module ships pollutionCap/pollutionCurve support but nothing enables it, and DESIGN.md's asymmetric formula is the root cause. → In src/resources/index.js make saturation the default rather than opt-in: set DEFAULTS.happiness.pollutionCap = 1.0 and pollutionCurve = 2.0 (penalty -> cap*(1-exp(-x/curve))), and add the same two keys to src/balance/config.js happiness so the balance owner sees them. Alternatively express pollution per capita (pollutionSum / max(1, pop/1000)) so a megacity's 100 smokestacks are not scored like a hamlet's. Update the DESIGN.md happiness line to match.

[medium] DEFAULTS in src/resources/index.js (lines ~90-104) claim to be a 'local mirror' of the balance numbers but have drifted: civicCap 1.0 vs config 1.25, pollutionScale 1 vs 0.2, unemploymentPenalty 0.4 vs 0.3, pop.growthRate 0.06 vs 0.08, power.brownoutFloor 0.25 vs 0.4. If src/balance/config.js ever fails to import, the game silently plays with a materially different balance (5x harsher pollution, 40% longer brownouts). → Either import config statically (import { config } from '../balance/config.js') and delete DEFAULTS, or sync the five numbers and add a one-line assertion in tools/economy-sim.mjs that DEFAULTS deep-equals the config sections it mirrors so drift fails the gauntlet.

[low] Negative global mods are treated inconsistently: computeDerived uses nonNeg(m.income, 1), which maps income:-3 to 0 (verified: income became $0/s), while core/mods.sanitizeMods maps the same value to 1. Only matters if a caller bypasses sanitizeMods, but the two policies disagree. → In src/resources/index.js replace the nonNeg(m.x, 1) reads for the multiplicative mods with a helper posOr1(v) that returns 1 when v is not finite OR v < 0, matching sanitizeMods.

[low] No unit tests exist for src/resources/ (no tests/ directory; only tools/verify.mjs and tools/economy-sim.mjs exercise it indirectly). The hand-check script I wrote found no bugs, but the module's contract (breakdown sums to gross, clamp bounds, baseInflow suppressed at pop==housing) is unprotected against regressions. → Add tests/resources.test.mjs (node --test) with the two synthetic-city cases above plus the empty/garbage/1e300 edge cases, asserting each derived field to 1e-9.

[low] At 1e308-scale inputs housing and popGrowth overflow to Infinity (count*housing*mods). Simulation's Number.isFinite guards on income/popGrowth prevent state corruption, but derived.housing/powerDemand = Infinity would reach the UI unfiltered. Purely theoretical at real-game magnitudes (sim tops out around 1e11 money). → Optional: after the summation loop, pass housing/jobs/powerCap/powerDemand/buildingIncome/upkeep through num(v, 0) or Math.min(v, 1e300) so every derived field is guaranteed finite.
issuesLeftAfterFix: docs/DESIGN.md happiness line still describes the linear pollution form (docs folder, not mine) — integrator should update it to: pollution = pollutionCap·(1 − exp(−Σ·pollutionScale / pollutionCurve)).
Drift assertion in tools/economy-sim.mjs not added (tools folder, not mine); covered by src/resources/resources.test.mjs instead.

economy-sim reports FAIL (stall + 23 flat) due to a concurrent change outside my folder: src/simulation/tuning.js legacyPower: 3 makes income ∝ legacy^3 while gain ∝ sqrt(earned), which diverges (legacy 9e123, income 2e72/s, prestige every 40 ticks from minute 52). Confirmed independent of my change: forcing linear pollution gives a bit-identical run. Zero errors in both verify and sim.

buildings.verdict: Clean, well-structured module with the best flavor writing in the project and zero errors; every building is bought and early cadence is tight. It fails the 8.5 bar on gameplay: the buildings' own pollution values, combined with a saturating civic curve, drive happiness to the 0.25 floor from prestige 21 onward and stretch cycles from 6 min to 138 min; fusion makes four of five power buildings pointless; and mid-game unlocks sit unaffordable for 10-14 minutes. Fix pollution saturation and fusion scale first, then tighten hospital/arcology/techpark unlocks.
issues: [high] Pollution is linear and uncapped while civic happiness saturates (config.happiness.civicCap 1.25), so the negative happiness values in src/buildings/data.js (factory -0.02, coal -0.03, refinery -0.05) eventually win outright. In logs/sim-gauntlet.json happiness ends each cycle at 1.99 (cycle 2) but slides monotonically: 1.07 (cycle 12), 0.63 (cycle 16), 0.37 (cycle 19), and is pinned at the 0.25 floor from cycle 21 on (final state: pollution 2.386 vs civic 1.25 + 0.2 mods; raw pollution sum -11.93 from 123 factories / 129 coal / 112 refineries). Income multiplier drops to 0.625 and growth crawls, so prestige cycle length explodes from 5-6 min (cycles 10-12) to 54, 80, 117, 138 min (cycles 21-24) — the exact opposite of DESIGN.md's 'each subsequent prestige cycle shorter'. The config.js comment calibrates pollutionScale for a '60 factory / 60 coal / 45 refinery' city; the sim buys twice that. → Make pollution saturate like civic does, or give each polluter a positive-happiness counterpart at the same tier. Concretely: in src/buildings/data.js drop coal to -0.015 and refinery to -0.03, and give techpark +0.05 / solar +0.03 / nuclear +0.02 (clean-power narrative) so late cities can neutralise their own smog; then add a 'pollutionCap' (e.g. 1.0) in resources so the penalty is 'cap*(1-exp(-sum/scale))' — mirroring civic. Re-run the 12h sim and require happiness >= 1.0 at the end of every cycle.

[medium] Fusion Reactor (2,000,000 MW for $400k, config override) obsoletes every other generator the instant it unlocks: coal 80 MW, solar 900 MW, nuclear 25,000 MW. Final state has powerCap 739,623,456 MW vs demand 225,273 MW (3,280x surplus). The sim still buys 129 coal / 125 solar / 126 nuclear only because bot.js scores powerGen*2 unconditionally; a human would never touch 4 of the 5 power cards after cycle 2, which turns the whole Power tab into dead weight for 90% of the game. → Either cut fusion powerGen to ~150,000 MW (6x nuclear, matching the ~5-10x step between other tiers) and raise late powerUse (arcology 500 -> 2,500, financial 800 -> 4,000, techpark 900 -> 4,500) so demand keeps pace with tier-4 cities, or give surplus power a use (e.g. derived.powerSurplus feeds a small income/happiness bonus) so generators stay purchases. Verify with the sim that powerCap/powerDemand stays under ~5x at end of run.

[medium] Unlock-to-affordable waits in the mid game are long: hospital unlocks at 16.1 min but is first bought at 30.0 (13.9 min wait), arcology 22.9 -> 37.0 (14.1 min), techpark 28.1 -> 39.5 (11.3), solar 12.8 -> 23.7 (10.9), mall 12.3 -> 22.1 (9.8). The 'newly unlocked -> glow' card then sits unaffordable for a quarter hour; first purchases go quiet between 23.7 and 30.0 min and again 30.0 -> 37.0 min, and there are no new buildings at all from minute 45 to the first prestige at ~50. → Bring unlock rules closer to the cost frontier: hospital unlock pop 2,500 -> 4,000 (or baseCost 60,000 -> 35,000), arcology pop 4,000 -> 6,000, techpark 5,000 -> 7,000, mall pop 600 -> 900, solar pop 1,000 -> 1,500. Target: unlock-to-first-purchase wait <= 5 min for every building (currently 9 of 20 exceed it).

[medium] No per-building count milestones (the Cookie Clicker / Antimatter Dimensions 'every 25 owned = x2' pattern), so a late-game building purchase at count 130 (cost 1.12^130 = 2.5e6x base) adds ~0.1% income. This is the source of the 39 'flat' issues in logs/sim-gauntlet.json (income grew <5% over 10 min, e.g. 1.20e9 -> 1.18e9 at t=14400) and part of why late cycles balloon. → Add a `tierBonus` field to building defs (e.g. every 25 owned multiplies that building's output by 1.5, exposed via mods.byBuilding in computeDerived) and surface the next threshold on the card ('12 more for x1.5'). This gives every building a reason to be bought toward a goal rather than by frontier price alone.

[low] Fusion's unlockAt is { pop: 100000, legacy: 1 } but src/ui/build.js unlockProgress only reads .pop, so a first-run player sees a bar toward '100,000 citizens' while the hint says 'or found a new city' (the realistic path). In practice nobody reaches 100k pop before first prestige (cycle-1 peak is ~52k at 48 min). → Set fusion unlockAt to { legacy: 1 } only and let the UI render 'Found a new city' as the progress label, or make the UI show the nearer of the two conditions.

[low] Commercial and industrial tiers 1-2 are nearly interchangeable in role: office (40 jobs, $4/s, $1,200) vs factory (20 jobs, $3/s, $500, -0.02 joy) is a jobs/cost ratio of 0.033 vs 0.040 with a small pollution tax; the only differentiator is the happiness sign, which is invisible for the first 20 minutes because civic easily covers it. Techpark (tier-3 industrial) even has positive happiness, blurring the category further. → Give the categories a mechanical hook beyond happiness sign: industrial income scaled by employed ratio (needs workers), commercial income scaled by pop (needs shoppers) — or at minimum make industrial jobs cheaper per $ and commercial income higher per job so the trade-off is visible on the card.

[low] DESIGN.md's building table is stale versus the live numbers (arcology 1.2e6 vs $120k in config.js, fusion 5e8 vs $400k, tier-4 unlocks 4,000-10,000 pop vs 5,000-20,000). The doc acknowledges this in a warning box but the table is still the canonical reference every builder reads. → Regenerate the table in docs/DESIGN.md from the resolved registry (a 20-line script over resolveBuilding) so the doc and config cannot drift.
issuesLeftAfterFix: Arcology (wait 9.1 min) and Tech Campus (6.5 min): their unlock rules AND base costs are set by config.buildings in src/balance/config.js (popUnlock 4000/5000), which my applyOverride must honour per the DESIGN contract. Balance should move arcology to pop 6,000 and techpark to pop 6,500 (bot pop timeline: 6,157 at min 28, first buys at 29.8/30.0).

[medium] Per-building count milestones (tierBonus): cannot be done inside src/buildings — simulation.foldMods only folds upgrade effects, milestones and prestige, and resources.computeDerived only reads mods.byBuilding. Needs an integrator seam: e.g. simulation folds `def.effect(mods, state, count)` for owned buildings (mirroring upgrades) or resources reads `def.tierBonus`; the buildings module can then ship the field and the UI the 'N more for x1.5' label.

[low] Commercial vs industrial mechanical hook (income scaled by pop vs employed ratio) lives in resources.computeDerived; office/factory income and baseCost are also config overrides, so only jobs were available to me and shifting them alone would just make factories strictly dominant. Left as is.

[low] docs/DESIGN.md building table regeneration: docs/ is outside my folder. Live registry differs from the table in powerGen/powerUse/happiness/unlock for 12 buildings after this pass; a resolveBuilding dump would regenerate it.

Economy sim pass:false (1 stall, 22 flat) is a legacy runaway independent of buildings: the identical stall occurs with the original data.js values on the current tree (logs/sim-fix-buildings-origvalues.json, legacy 3.4e125). Cause: src/simulation/tuning.js default legacyPower 3 (income multiplier (1+0.04·legacy)^3) combined with config.prestige.exponent 0.5 (gain ∝ √earned) makes gain ∝ legacy^1.5, so cycles collapse to ~6 s and legacy overflows to 1e147. Simulation/balance need to bring legacyPower to 1 (or exponent back to 0.35) before any 12h sim can pass.

upgrades.verdict: Solid, well-engineered module with zero errors, exact mod-only effects, legible descriptions and a good first-hour cadence, but it fails the premium bar on one real gameplay flaw: the 41-upgrade tree is finite and priced far below late-game income, so after roughly 4.5 hours every prestige cycle exhausts all upgrades in 2-3 minutes and the player idles with nothing to buy for the rest of each cycle (source of all 39 flat-income flags in the sim). Add repeatable or legacy-scaled late rungs, lift the three sub-25% effects, and fix the additive-vs-multiplier happiness desc mismatch to reach 8.5+.
issues: [major] No late-game upgrade horizon. In logs/sim-gauntlet.json, from about legacy 300 onward (cycle 17 of 24, ~4.5h in) the bot owns all 40 upgrades by minute 2-3 of every cycle and then has nothing to buy for the remaining 30-130 min of each cycle; all 39 'flat' income issues fall in those stretches. The top rung (planetary-charter, $5e8 in config.js) costs 1/8 of a second of the final $4.0e9/s income. → Add a repeatable/tiered rung to src/upgrades/data.js: e.g. 'Civic Bonds I-X' (All income +25% each, cost 1e9 x 10^n) and 'Skyline Expansion I-V' (All housing +50%), or make ai-governance/planetary-charter scale cost with legacy (cost * (1 + legacy/50)). Target: at least one unowned affordable-within-10-minutes upgrade at every point of a 12h sim.

[moderate] Three effects fall below the +25% meaningfulness bar: grant-writing (+10% income, data.js line ~182), tax-software (+15%, line ~193), bulk-permits (-5% cost, line ~320). Bulk Permits is the weakest: -5% cost is a rounding error against 1.12-1.15 cost growth. → Bump grant-writing to +20% and tax-software to +25% (or merge them into one +30%), and raise bulk-permits to -15% cost (prefab-construction then -20%).

[moderate] 'Parks give x2 happiness' (green-belts), 'Schools give +50% happiness' (modern-curriculum) and 'Hospitals give +50% happiness' (preventive-care) are implemented as additive constants (happinessOf('park', 0.05) etc.) that only equal x2/+50% because the base values in src/buildings/data.js happen to be 0.05/0.08/0.12. Any config.buildings override of a civic building's happiness silently makes the desc text lie. → Either add a byBuilding.happinessMult field in src/core/mods.js and have resources multiply def.happiness by it, or reword the desc to the literal number ('Parks give +0.05 happiness each').

[moderate] Cadence gaps in the first cycle: no upgrade between minutes 10-13 and 31-37 (sim samples), and the first upgrade lands at tick 1160 (116 s) versus the DESIGN.md target of ~1 min and config.js's own claim of ~66 s. → Pull express-transit's unlock from pop 200 to pop 120 and night-shift from 10 factories to 6 to fill the 10-13 gap; add a ~$100k-$150k global rung (e.g. 'Regional Airport: All income +30%' at pop 3000) for the 31-37 gap; drop zoning-reform's unlock from 5 houses to 4 so the first upgrade lands near 60 s.

[minor] smart-grid is gated solely behind the brownout milestone (or a live powerRatio < 1). A player who keeps the grid ahead of demand never sees it; the Node sim bot went 12h/24 cycles without it. The verify browser run did buy it, so this is a design choice, not a bug, but an upgrade that rewards a mistake is odd. → Add an alternative trigger in data.js: unlock: any(brownout rule, hasBuilt('windmill', 6), (s,d)=>d && d.powerDemand >= 40).

[minor] dynasty-ledger's '+10% per legacy point (max +200%)' cap of 20 legacy is hit by the 5th prestige (legacy 5 -> 10 -> 15 -> 20 in the sim), so for 95% of the game it is a flat +200% with a misleadingly dynamic description. → Raise the cap to 100 points (max +1000%) with a smaller per-point value (+5%), or replace the cap with a sqrt curve: mods.income *= 1 + 0.5 * Math.sqrt(legacy).

[minor] orbital-solar and superconductor-grid share the identical unlock (pop 100k or fusion) and both sit in the same 5e6-1.3e7 band, so they appear together rather than as a sequence; likewise arcology-gardens and planetary-charter both carry cost 1e10 in data.js and depend on config.js to separate them. → Give superconductor-grid its own trigger (hasBuilt('nuclear', 4) or owns orbital-solar) and stagger the data.js defaults so the file is self-consistent without config overrides.

simulation.verdict: The simulation code itself is close to release quality: correct fixed-step integration with NaN-proof clamps, tick cost 0.005 ms avg / 0.10 ms p99 (100x under budget), zero errors across 10k browser ticks and a 432k-tick economy sim, allocation-free milestone/gate loops, and a clean event surface the UI actually consumes. What holds it below the bar is design, not bugs: the prestige loop is weak at both ends. At $1M the game lights up a 'Found a new city' button that trades a 20-minute city for +4% and $21, and after roughly 12 prestiges (about 2 hours) the linear +4%/point payoff stops keeping pace with ^0.35 gain, so late cycles stretch from 6 to 117 minutes and end in 30-100 minute plateaus where income actually falls as buildings are added (happiness pinned at 0.25 by uncapped pollution). Add a brownout-log guard inconsistency and log wipe on prestige as polish nits. Fix the prestige curve and pollution cap and this module is an easy 8.5-9.
issues: [high] The first prestige is a trap. canPrestige fires at totalEarned >= $1M (src/simulation/prestige.js:55) with gain = floor((1e6/1e6)^0.35) = 1 legacy, worth +4% income and +$21 start money (210 * 0.1). The UI (src/ui/hero.js:227-233) fills the bar to 100%, lights the button `is-ready`, and says 'Founding now grants 1 legacy: +4% income ... forever.' A player who accepts resets a ~20-minute city (pop ~3.5k, income ~$2.4k/s) for a replay that is not measurably faster. The bot only prestiges at >= 5 points (src/core/bot.js:17 prestigeMin=5, i.e. $99M, minute 48) precisely because 1 point is worthless. Top-tier incrementals make the first reset transformative (Cookie Clicker heavenly chips, AD infinity). → Either make the first points count (e.g. incomePerLegacy 0.25 with exponent 0.35, or a first-prestige bonus: legacyIncomeMult = 1 + 0.04*legacy + (legacy>0 ? 0.5 : 0)), or raise the gating so the button only arms at a meaningful haul: in prestige.js canPrestige() require prestigeGain() >= 3 (and set config.prestige.minGain: 3) and have hero.js label the bar 'next legacy point at' using the already-exported but unused nextLegacyAt().

[high] The prestige loop runs dry after ~2 hours. Legacy income is linear (+4%/pt, prestige.js:71) while legacy gain is totalEarned^0.35, so required earnings for the bot's next meaningful reset grow ~L^2.86 against income growing ~L. logs/sim-gauntlet.json prestigeTicks: cycle length bottoms at 5.9 min (prestige 11-13) then balloons 7, 8, 9, 12, 16, 24, 36, 54, 80, 117 min. From prestige ~12 onward every cycle ends in a 30-100 minute plateau (all 39 sim 'flat' issues: income grew <5% over 10 min, e.g. run 23: income 3.55e9 @3 min -> 2.75e9 @20 min -> 2.93e9 @48 min while buildings go 1524 -> 2178). The player has all 40 upgrades and all 20 buildings by minute 4 of a late run; nothing new appears for the remaining 9+ hours. → Give legacy a super-linear or multiplicative payoff and/or deeper sinks: e.g. legacyIncomeMult = (1 + 0.04*L) * 1.02^L, or make legacy spendable on a permanent upgrade tree (a 'legacy' cost field consumed by performPrestige and tracked in state.prestige.spent, which already exists but is never written). Also extend the milestone list past money-1t / pop-1m with rewards, since the last rewarded milestone (pop-1m) is reached inside the second hour.

[medium] Income declines as the city grows in every late cycle because happiness pins at the 0.25 floor: pollution is linear and uncapped (src/resources/math.js pollutionPenalty with cap=0; src/balance/config.js sets pollutionScale 0.2 but no pollutionCap/pollutionCurve) while the civic bonus saturates at civicCap 1.25. Run 23 samples: happiness 1.99 -> 0.887 (3 min) -> 0.25 (23 min) and stays there; income falls from 3.55e9 to 2.75e9 while buildings rise. Buying more of the game makes the number go down, which is the opposite of the genre promise; a human cannot fix it with parks because civic is capped and pollution is not. → Set config.happiness.pollutionCap (e.g. 1.0) and pollutionCurve (e.g. 3) so the resources saturation path in math.js is actually used, or make civicCap scale with civic building tiers. Add a sim assertion in tools/economy-sim.mjs: income must not fall >10% over 10 min while buildings increase.

[medium] watchGrid() (src/simulation/index.js:229-238) logs 'Brownout. The grid is running at 40%: income and growth are dimmed.' whenever powerDemand > 0 and ratio < 0.95, with no powerCap > 0 guard. A cottage draws 1 MW (src/buildings/data.js:31) and the windmill only unlocks once something draws power, so a player who buys a cottage first sees a brownout warning within the first second, before a generator can exist. milestones.js isBrownout() explicitly requires powerCap > 0 for exactly this reason; the log path is inconsistent with it. → In watchGrid use the same predicate: `if (derived.powerDemand > 0 && derived.powerCap > 0 && ratio < BROWNOUT_ENTER)`, or export isBrownout from milestones.js and share it.

[low] performPrestige wipes the city log: resetState -> loadState({}) rebuilds state.log = [] (src/core/state.js:67-70), so the only line left after founding is the prestige line itself. Milestone history, the 'Welcome, Mayor' line, and the run's story are gone; state.time/tick also reset so log timestamps restart at 0. → In performPrestige capture `const log = state.log.slice(-20)` before resetState and restore it (or pass keepLog into resetState), and add a divider entry such as 'City #N founded'.

[low] Fallback constants drift from the shipped balance: prestige.js DEFAULTS = {exponent 0.5, incomePerLegacy 0.05, startMoneyPerLegacy 0.5, startMoney 50} vs config.js {0.35, 0.04, 0.1, 210}; hero.js also hardcodes 0.05 as its fallback (line 217). index.js additionally re-implements threshold reading in prestigeThreshold() instead of calling prestigeConfig(). If config.prestige is ever missing, the sim, UI, and gate disagree on the rules. → Delete prestigeThreshold()/tapSeconds() in index.js in favour of prestigeConfig(cfg).threshold, and sync DEFAULTS to the config values (or import config defaults from one place, e.g. export DEFAULTS from balance/config.js).

[low] nextLegacyAt() is exported from simulation/index.js but nothing consumes it (grep: only defined/exported), while the prestige panel shows a bar that stays pinned at 100% from $1M onward with no hint of when the next point lands. Also tap() emits no event, so any future UI feedback (toast, particle) must rely on the return value. → Have hero.js render 'Next legacy point at $X' from nextLegacyAt(state) and switch the bar to progress toward the next point once can===true; emit('tap', {gain}) from tap() for symmetry with the other actions.

ui.verdict: Excellent foundation with a genuinely premium look and a clean, cheap render loop, and the dashboard demonstrably grows across the run; it falls just short of the 8.5 bar because the toast stack overlays the sidebar (and at 1100px, buy buttons) for seconds at a time in normal play, the whole app is an aria-live region that floods screen readers, and small-label contrast is under AA. Fix the toast placement and the #app aria-live and this passes.
issues: [medium] Toast stack covers interactive UI. .toasts (styles.css:1801) is fixed bottom-right with max-width 360px and MAX_VISIBLE=4 (toast.js:6); measured host box 1062-1422px vs sidebar column 1065-1424px at 1440, so a milestone+unlock burst (common: 'Milestone: ...' x2 + '8 new buildings unlocked' + '9 new upgrades available', ~320px tall) hides the Milestones panel and City Log for 5.6s+ each. At 1100x800 the same stack (left=722) also covers the Residential Tower Buy/Sell button in the build column (see scratchpad live-1100-end.png, live-1100-scrolled.png). → Move the host to bottom-center of the build column (e.g. .toasts { left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); bottom: 18px; max-width: 380px }) or top-center below the topbar, drop MAX_VISIBLE to 3, and fold multi-unlock toasts into one line with 'and N more' instead of listing 9 names.

[medium] index.html:14 puts aria-live="polite" on the whole #app. Money, income, clock and population text nodes change every animation frame (topbar.js update), so screen readers are flooded with announcements continuously; this makes the game unusable with a screen reader and defeats the properly scoped aria-live on .toasts (toast.js:10). → Remove aria-live from #app in index.html; keep it only on .toasts and optionally on a small status region for milestone text.

[low] --text-3 (#6b7489, styles.css:18) measures ~4.0:1 against the panel ground (~#0e1220) and is used for 10-11px text (chip-label 10px, stat-label 10.5px, ms-pct 11px, ucard-cat 9.5px, log-time 11px). WCAG AA needs 4.5:1 at these sizes; the 9.5px uppercase upgrade category label is the hardest to read. → Raise --text-3 to ~#7d879c (about 5:1) and bump .ucard-cat to 10.5px.

[low] At 1100px the locked-teaser row clips: bcard-name truncates to 'Undiscovered residential buil...' and .unlock-meta (styles.css:1331, nowrap, margin-left:auto) is cut off at '272 / 4,0' because it has no flex-shrink:0 and the row is overflow-hidden; .next-desc (styles.css:895) is nowrap+ellipsis so 'Five hundred citizens. The county sends a letter.' becomes 'The county sen...' in a 320px hero column. → Add flex-shrink:0 to .unlock-meta and let .bcard-name shrink first (min-width:0 already there); change .next-desc to a 2-line -webkit-line-clamp instead of nowrap.

[low] Category tab bar wraps to a second row at 1440 once all five categories unlock (tab tops measured 138,138,138,138,175): 'Civic' sits alone on row two, breaking the header rhythm in the primary panel. → Tighten .tab padding to 5px 8px and .tabs gap to 3px, or hide .tab-label below 1300px column width and keep icon+count, so five tabs fit in the 580px build column.

[low] Power chip's .power-bar (styles.css:595) renders a full-width yellow fill when supply == demand, and the happiness chip's .is-warn border is also yellow (--warn), so the topbar shows two yellow-highlighted chips in a healthy state (end screenshots: '1.12K / 815 MW, 300 MW spare' has a solid yellow underline). Yellow reads as warning; it dilutes the real brownout signal. → Only paint the power-bar when ratio < 1 (or colour it --money at >=1), and reserve --warn for is-warn/is-bad states.

[low] The 'tap the city to collect' pill (.city-hint, hero.js:711) is permanent; after a few taps it is noise on the hero panel, and in the endgame the hero card also sits with ~80px of dead space below City Stats while the build column has ~240px empty at 1440x900. → Hide .city-hint once state.stats.clicks >= 5 (fade out), and let .col-build panel-build flex:1 so the locked teaser/cards fill the column, or move City Log under Build when the sidebar overflows.

[low] index.html:10-11 loads Inter and JetBrains Mono from fonts.googleapis.com at runtime; first paint shows system-ui/Consolas then swaps (FOUT), and offline play renders with fallback fonts. → Self-host the two families as woff2 (font-display: swap with preload), or accept the fallbacks and pin their metrics with size-adjust.
issuesLeftAfterFix: index.html (outside src/ui) still contains aria-live="polite" on #app and the three fonts.googleapis/gstatic <link> tags; both are neutralized at runtime by src/ui (attribute removed before content mounts; bundled families win the stack and the Google woff2 files are no longer fetched), but the integrator should delete them from index.html

Toasts can still cover the bottom of a long build-card list for up to ~5.6 s (max 3, click-to-dismiss, hover-pause) - this is the bottom-of-build-column placement the critic proposed; sidebar and buy buttons are clear in all measured cases

tools/economy-sim.mjs --ticks 216000 reports pass:false (stall at t=41920 with money 1.9e119, income 2.5e72, legacy 9e123, 24 flat/stall issues) with errors: []; the Node sim never imports src/ui and src/balance, src/simulation, src/upgrades, src/buildings, src/resources and src/core were modified by other builders during this session (mtimes 18:52-18:58), so this is a balance/simulation regression outside my folder

save.verdict: The save module is genuinely hardened: every tamper, private-mode, quota, round-trip and offline scenario I ran passed with zero console errors, and the offline catch-up is fast, capped and correctly persisted. It misses PASS only on a real balance flaw - the configured 50% offline efficiency is never applied to the simulated path, so offline earnings are 2x the documented rate on fast machines and device-dependent on slow ones - plus small migration/save-on-prestige gaps. Fix the efficiency rule and this is a 9.
issues: [medium] src/save/index.js: offlineEfficiency (config 0.5) is applied only to the analytic remainder in finishCatchUp(); ticks simulated by runChunk() pay 100%. With the 1500ms budget a full 8h cap simulates in ~1s on a desktop (measured 28800s in 1069ms, earned = income x 28800 exactly), so the documented 50% offline efficiency is effectively dead, and a slow phone that hits the budget gets half the reward for the remainder - offline payout is device-dependent. → Pick one rule and apply it to both paths: e.g. in runChunk() record money before game.step(n) and scale the delta by cfg.offlineEfficiency (state.res.money = before + (after-before)*eff, same for stats.totalEarned/prestige.lifetimeEarned), or set save.offlineEfficiency to 1 in balance/config.js and drop the analytic scaling. Add a comment in config.js stating which.

[low] src/save/index.js runMigrations(): when a MIGRATIONS[v] step is missing the loop breaks but st.version is still stamped STATE_VERSION, so a half-migrated save is treated as current forever and can never be re-migrated. → Only assign st.version = v after the loop; if v < STATE_VERSION, console.warn('[save] no migration from v'+v) and either keep the old version number or fail parseSave so the raw save is parked under CORRUPT_KEY.

[low] src/save/index.js coerceShape(): a partially corrupt save (e.g. res.money non-numeric) loads with money 0 rather than startMoney, and unknown building ids (tested {fake:2}) are kept in state.buildings indefinitely. → In coerceShape, drop building/upgrade ids not present in registry.buildings/registry.upgrades (import getBuilding/getUpgrade), and in loadFromStorage set state.res.money = cfg.startMoney when the money key was stripped by coercion.

[low] src/save/index.js: no save is triggered on major state changes (prestige, milestone); only the 30s interval and unload hooks. A tab crash within 30s of pressing 'Found a new city' silently loses the prestige (or worse, replays the pre-prestige city on reload). → In init(), add game.events.on('prestige', () => autosaveOn() && save('prestige')) (and optionally 'upgrade'), reusing the MIN_AUTO_GAP_MS collapse.

[low] Offline catch-up emits milestone toasts during simulation, so in offline-toast.png the 'While you were away' toast lands last, beneath two 'Milestone' toasts and partly faded at the viewport bottom - the most important notice is the least visible. → Either emit 'offline' before running the simulated chunks with a placeholder and update it, or have the save module set info.catchingUp and let ui/index.js suppress/queue milestone toasts while game.saveInfo.catchingUp is true, then show the offline toast first.
issuesLeftAfterFix: Offline toast still lands beneath milestone toasts in the screenshot (logs/screenshot-fix-save-offline.png) because ui/index.js does not yet consult game.saveInfo.catchingUp or the new 'catchup' event; the save module cannot intercept simulation's milestone emits without editing src/ui or src/core
The critic's suggested comment in src/balance/config.js stating which efficiency rule applies was not added (not my folder); the rule is documented at the top of src/save/index.js instead
economy-sim FAIL (legacy 9e123 runaway, income flat at 2.5e72/s, 24 balance issues) is a shared balance/upgrades state affecting every builder's run identically and is not reachable from src/save

issues: [high] Happiness collapses to the 0.25 floor in the late game and the civic lever stops working. config.happiness.pollutionScale 0.2 applies a LINEAR, uncapped pollution penalty while civicBonus saturates at civicCap 1.25: at the 12 h city (123 factories, 129 coal, 112 refineries) pollution = 2.39 > 1 + 1.25 + 0.1, so happiness sits at the floor from cycle 21 (~6 h) onward and drifts down from cycle 13; income declines inside late cycles (e.g. cycle 12 peak 1.19e8 → 1.10e8) and all 39 sim 'flat' warnings occur after 3 h. The config comment only scopes the scale to '90 minutes of greedy play'. → In src/balance/config.js happiness block add `pollutionCap: 1.0, pollutionCurve: 1.0` (src/resources/math.js pollutionPenalty already supports both; resources reads them each tick). Verified by mutating config in memory: min happiness after 10 min goes 0.25 → 0.52, never floors in 12 h, final income 4.0e9 → 1.27e10. Update the pollutionScale comment to describe the saturating curve.

[high] Prestige cadence reverses instead of accelerating: after cycle 12 (3.6 h) durations grow 5.8 → 6 → 7.2 → 8.4 → 9.2 → 8.7 → 11.7 → 16.5 → 24.2 → 36 → 54.2 → 80 → 117.4 min, then a 139-min cycle never completes. With config.prestige.exponent 0.35 the earnings needed for a meaningful (+25%) legacy haul grow as (0.25·L)^2.86 while income only grows ×(1 + 0.04·L); a fixed-gain player gets shrinking cycles only because each reset becomes worthless (+5 legacy at L=2779 is +0.18% income). → Set config.prestige.exponent 0.35 → 0.5 (the DESIGN.md default). Verified in memory: cycles keep shrinking to 2.0 min at ~2.5 h, 46 prestiges in 12 h (vs 24), final legacy 265k, final income 7.5e11/s; combined with the pollution cap: 49 prestiges, 3.0e12/s. Cycles still lengthen after ~3 h under any config value because incomePerLegacy is additive-linear — to keep cadence accelerating, applyPrestigeMods (src/simulation/prestige.js) needs a compounding bonus (e.g. ×1.02^legacy with a soft cap) or legacy needs a spend sink; flag as a design follow-up outside config.

[medium] Content horizon ends at ~3 h of a 12 h run. 40/41 upgrades are owned by cycle 9; the legacy ladder (legacy-archive $5k, founders-blueprints $30k, veteran-planners $80k, dynasty-ledger $150k) is fully bought by cycle 3; AI Governance ($5e7) and Planetary Charter ($5e8), described in config.js as 'the horizon', are bought around cycle 9. From then on every cycle is buy-the-same-20-buildings with income flat to declining (39 'flat' flags). → Add late legacy rungs to config.upgrades (and matching entries in src/upgrades/data.js gated on legacy ≥ 50 / 250 / 1000 at $1e7 / $1e9 / $1e11), and re-price ai-governance to ~$5e8 and planetary-charter to ~$2e10 so they land in cycles 15–20 rather than 9.

[low] Opening 80 s is the only slow stretch: startMoney $210 is spent in 4 s on 5 buildings, then income is $0.8–1.1/s against $50–58 items, giving waits of 38 s (4 s → 42 s) and 42 s (42 s → 84 s) before the first shop; first upgrade lands at 116 s, not the '~66 s' the config.js header claims. Cookie Clicker gets the first purchase moving within ~15 s. → Raise config.economy.startMoney 210 → 260 (or drop shop baseCost 50 → 35) so the $50 shop is affordable in the opening spree and the first paycheck starts at ~5 s; correct the header comment to the measured 116 s.

[low] The brownout mechanic is nearly invisible to a careful player: powerRatio never drops below 0.957 in 12 h (1.3% of steps < 1, 2.8% in cycle 0), the DESIGN.md 'first brownout ~3 min' beat never happens in the sim, and Smart Grid — the only never-purchased item — cannot unlock without one (its unlock is milestone 'brownout' or powerRatio < 1). The browser bot does trip it (8% share), so this is partly a bot artifact. → Give smart-grid a second unlock path in src/upgrades/data.js (`derived.powerDemand >= 20`, i.e. when coal unlocks) so a competent player still sees it; optionally raise config.buildings.windmill.costGrowth 1.5 → 1.6 so the windmill→coal gap creates a brief, visible brownout around minute 3.

[low] Documentation drift: config.js header says first upgrade ~66 s (measured 116 s) and cycles '48 → 25 → 21 → 17 → 16 → 14' (measured 49.9 → 26.4 → 21.6 → 19.7 → 17.3 → 15.1); DESIGN.md pacing paragraph still says $1M at 35–50 min and 1k pop ~8 min (measured 20.5 min and 12.8 min). → Update the config.js header to the measured values (first upgrade 116 s, 1k pop 12.8 min, $1M 20.5 min, first prestige 49.9 min, cycle list above) and replace the DESIGN.md pacing paragraph with a pointer to those numbers.
